guidance.procedure: Resolve the relation by matching the actor, operative action, protected object, modality, trigger, exception and quantifier. Entailment requires language establishing the proposition; Contradiction requires an incompatible operative rule. Related language, silence, or a missing permission is not automatically contradiction. Then collect every complete responsive provision, including any lead-in, definition, exception introduction, continuation or referenced trigger needed to preserve force and scope. Include repeated provisions that independently resolve the issue; exclude headings and merely contextual clauses. Search the whole contract before selecting NotMentioned, and return no evidence for that label because a local excerpt cannot prove absence.

Read the entire operative definition. Technical-only coverage requires an exhaustive subject-matter definition confined to technical categories; business, financial, commercial, personnel, customer, contractual or marketing matter contradicts it. Transmission form does not determine subject matter. For explicit identification, ask whether every protected disclosure must be marked, designated, identified or confirmed. Coverage based alternatively on reasonable understanding, confidential circumstances, or protection whether or not marked contradicts universal identification. For verbal coverage, require an operative oral, spoken or verbal mode, or an unmistakably comprehensive tangible-and-intangible formulation; include any identification or later-confirmation conditions.

Analyze the disposition trigger separately from what may remain afterward. A duty tied to termination, expiration, project completion, abandoned discussions or another stated ending event supports termination-related return or destruction; a request-only duty does not inherit a trigger from a separate duration clause. Return alone is sufficient. For post-disposition possession, an express archival, legal, backup, regulatory, dispute or record-retention exception supports possession. An exhaustive command covering all protected information and copies, without a retention exception, contradicts it; a command limited to documents or another subset is unresolved. Include the complete trigger, all disposition alternatives and every applicable carve-out.

Require an operative disclosure or access permission and identify its recipient class. Employees support employee sharing. Consultants, advisers, contractors, agents, affiliates and comparable outside representatives support third-party sharing only when the clause actually authorizes them to receive the information; a definition or description of status is not permission. Preserve need-to-know, purpose, consent and confidentiality conditions. An express ban reaching the class, with disclosure available only after separate approval or accession, opposes present permission. A generic disclosure ban that does not address the class is unresolved. Exclude neighboring security, password and market-restriction provisions.

Locate the particular exception or permission and its governing introduction. Independent development requires development without use of, reference to, benefit from or access to protected information; public-domain, compelled-disclosure and third-party-source clauses do not substitute for it. Third-party acquisition requires information received, furnished, obtained or acquired from a lawful outside source not bound by confidentiality or transmission restrictions; outgoing disclosure permission concerns a different action. Include all stated conditions. A direct prohibition opposes the proposition; absence of the particular limb remains unresolved.

Keep entitlement separate from permitted use. No-rights entailment requires an express denial of license, title, ownership, intellectual-property rights, right of use or another interest; sole ownership is sufficient only when the clause also excludes recipient rights. A purpose-limited permission does not contradict a denial of proprietary rights. Limited-use entailment requires an operative sole-purpose limitation or prohibition on other use, including a construction clause preserving only a purpose-bound use right. Ownership, return, nondisclosure and security duties alone do not establish limited use. Scan for and include every independent operative use restriction.

For reverse engineering, require an operative ban on reverse engineering, decompiling, disassembling, reconstruction or equivalent analysis of materials embodying protected information; a copying ban alone is insufficient. For copying, distinguish permission from prohibition: an express right, a necessary-copy exception, a consent-based exception or permission to retain a copy supports copying in some circumstances. An unqualified no-copy or no-retention rule opposes it. Legend preservation and storage controls merely regulate existing copies unless they also authorize or prohibit creation. Include the actor-bearing lead-in and any exception governing the verb series.

Require both legal compulsion and an operative warning duty. The trigger may be law, regulation, subpoena, court order or legal process, and the notice may occur in a later sentence. Permission to comply with law, a compelled-disclosure exclusion, or disclosure to a regulator without a notice duty is unresolved rather than contradiction. Preserve timing and legality qualifications, and include the complete trigger-plus-notice sequence; protective-order cooperation belongs only when it continues that sequence.

Treat the protected object separately for each proposition. Agreement secrecy requires operative protection of the agreement, its existence or terms, negotiations, their status, discussions or the contemplated transaction; confidentiality of exchanged information and an entire-agreement clause are irrelevant. Non-solicitation requires a ban on soliciting, recruiting, hiring, inducing departure or targeted contact with specified employees, consultants or other representatives; customer or market restraints alone do not suffice. Survival requires substantive duties to continue after termination or an express post-termination period; a fixed agreement term or liability only for earlier breaches does not preserve the duties. Include class, duration, exceptions and referenced substantive provisions needed for scope.

Read the complete operative definition and analyze subject matter, identification, and transmission mode separately. Technical-only coverage requires an exhaustive definition confined to technical categories; business, financial, commercial, personnel, customer, contractual, or marketing matter contradicts it. Explicit identification requires every protected disclosure to be marked, designated, identified, or confirmed; alternative coverage through reasonable understanding, confidential circumstances, or protection whether or not marked contradicts that universal requirement. Verbal coverage requires an express oral, spoken, or verbal mode, or genuinely comprehensive tangible-and-intangible language; generic references to all information, materials, or forms alone are insufficient. Include the definition's lead-in, alternatives, and any oral-identification or later-confirmation conditions.

Current observations repeatedly confused broad or unmarked definitions with universal identification, so the procedure now expressly separates subject matter, marking, and transmission mode.

Confidential Information: any information disclosed by one Party (the ‘Discloser’) to another party (the ‘Recipient’) relating directly or indirectly to the Project, which is identified by the disclosing Party, either orally or in writing, as confidential, either at the time of disclosure or, if disclosed orally, confirmed in writing within thirty (30) days following the original disclosure.

“Confidential Information” includes, without limitation, design documents, trade secrets, files, marketing and business plans, documentation, reports, projections, interpretations, forecasts, records (including information regarding the disclosing party’s businesses, customers, strategies, operations, finances, technology, data, processes, methodologies, know-how, existing or future products, services, applications and methods of operation (including how such methods are developed, conducted or operated)) and all other information, whether in written, oral, encoded, electronic or other tangible or intangible form, and whether or not labeled, marked or otherwise identified as “Confidential” upon disclosure thereof, relating to the disclosing party’s products and businesses, and any other information that would, if disclosed to any actual or potential competitors of the disclosing party, give or increase those competitors’ advantage over the disclosing party or directly or indirectly harm the disclosing party’s business.
